How It Works

How Professional Medical Office Cleaning Works

Our medical office cleaning process follows a systematic, six-step protocol designed to maximize pathogen elimination and provide verifiable documentation of results. Every step is performed by trained, background-checked technicians.

1
Clinical Area Terminal Cleaning

Exam rooms receive terminal cleaning — thorough decontamination of all surfaces within the patient zone including exam tables, countertops, equipment exteriors, light switches, door handles, and chairs. EPA-registered hospital-grade disinfectants are applied with verified dwell times.

2
Waiting Area and Reception

Patient-facing areas receive daily deep cleaning including seating sanitization, magazine and literature area maintenance, reception counter disinfection, glass cleaning, and floor care. These areas form patients' first impression of your practice.

3
Restroom Sanitization

Medical office restrooms are cleaned and disinfected with hospital-grade products, with particular attention to ADA-accessible fixtures, specimen collection areas (where applicable), and high-touch surfaces. Supply replenishment is verified at every service.

4
High-Touch Surface Protocol

Door handles, light switches, elevator buttons, handrails, check-in kiosks, and payment terminals are disinfected using EPA-registered products with documented dwell times. These surfaces are the primary vectors for pathogen transmission in healthcare settings.

5
Biohazard-Safe Waste Handling

Regulated medical waste is handled according to OSHA standards — proper segregation, containment in labeled receptacles, and coordination with licensed waste hauling services. Sharps containers are monitored but not serviced (licensed disposal required).

6
ATP Verification and Documentation

ATP bioluminescence testing verifies disinfection effectiveness on representative surfaces. All cleaning events are documented through JaniTrack with timestamped photos, ATP readings, products used, and technician identification for compliance audit readiness.

FAQ

Medical Office Cleaning FAQ — White Plains, NY

Common questions about medical office cleaning services in White Plains.

What is medical office cleaning?+
Medical office cleaning is specialized janitorial and disinfection service for healthcare environments that must comply with OSHA's Bloodborne Pathogens Standard, follow CDC environmental cleaning guidelines, use EPA-registered hospital-grade disinfectants, and implement terminal cleaning protocols for clinical areas. It differs from standard commercial cleaning in its regulatory requirements, product specifications, documentation standards, and the need for HIPAA-aware personnel.
Are your medical cleaning protocols OSHA compliant?+
Yes. All GreenPoint medical facility protocols meet OSHA Bloodborne Pathogens Standard (29 CFR 1910.1030) requirements including documented cleaning procedures for surfaces that may contact blood or OPIM, proper PPE for cleaning staff, EPA-registered hospital-grade disinfectant use with verified dwell times, employee training records, and exposure control plan documentation. Our JaniTrack system creates the compliance audit trail that OSHA inspectors require.
How do you prevent cross-contamination between exam rooms?+
We use color-coded microfiber systems (different colors for clinical surfaces vs. restrooms vs. common areas), dedicated supplies per room, terminal cleaning protocols between patients, and ATP bioluminescence testing to verify disinfection effectiveness. Cleaning staff are trained in the sequence of clean-to-contaminated area progression that prevents transferring pathogens between spaces.
Do you handle biohazard waste?+
We handle biohazard-safe waste segregation and containment according to OSHA standards — ensuring regulated medical waste is properly separated from general waste and placed in labeled, leak-proof containers. We coordinate with licensed medical waste hauling services for disposal. Sharps containers are monitored for fill level but require licensed disposal services.
Is your staff HIPAA trained?+
Yes. Every GreenPoint crew member assigned to medical facilities receives HIPAA awareness training covering PHI handling protocols, document confidentiality, and proper conduct in areas where patient information may be visible. Staff sign confidentiality agreements and undergo comprehensive background checks. We execute Business Associate Agreements with healthcare clients as standard practice.
How much does medical office cleaning cost?+
Medical office cleaning typically ranges from $0.12-$0.25 per square foot per cleaning visit — higher than standard commercial cleaning due to compliance requirements, hospital-grade products, terminal cleaning protocols, and documentation standards. A typical 3,000 sq ft medical office cleaned 5 days per week runs approximately $1,800-$3,500 per month. Pricing is customized based on exam room count, specialty type, and scope during a complimentary facility walkthrough.
Can you clean during patient hours?+
Yes. We offer day porter services for waiting areas, restrooms, and reception areas during patient hours, ensuring these spaces maintain presentation quality throughout the day. Exam rooms and clinical areas receive terminal cleaning after hours to avoid disrupting patient care. This dual-service model keeps patient-facing areas clean during operations while providing thorough clinical cleaning when the practice is closed.
